2026/10/11 | 10:41 PM » 100 questions for webmasters

questionnaire from mouseling.net; questions can be found here

1. Please introduce yourself.
hey. i go by a variety of different names in online spaces, but you can call me by my site name (strife) or by the name d.
2. How long have you been making websites?
i got into webdev back in august 2025.
3. And what got you into the hobby?
i had to go digging through my message history for this, but i believe it was this video by angieblah on youtube. i can't recall the specifics of what i was doing at the time, but this video mentioned that nekoweb didn't allow AI scraping, which interested me. then i dove into the hobby on a whim, teaching myself html/css on the fly.
4. What kind of website are you most interested in?
i like sites with a mishmash of content, whether it be blog entries, essays, art, resources, etc. i think it's interesting seeing the kinds of things people want to put on their personal websites.
5. What's your workflow? Do you plan your websites out thoroughly or do you come up with the design as you go along?
it's all done as i go along. my graphic design skills are kind of shit, so i start by thinking of what kind of content i wanted to have on my site first and work from there.
6. Please link to your biggest inspirations.
for the current iteration of this site at the time i'm writing this, my main inspiration started off with the 98.css CSS library.
7. What's your favourite part about making websites?
the problem-solving. it's incredibly fun being forced to troubleshoot and learn things on the go since i never learned the fundamentals of html/css. i love the process of having to search for answers.
8. And the thing you struggle with the most?
also the problem-solving. but the nekoweb discord is incredibly friendly and receptive to coding help questions, so i haven't run into too many roadblocks.
9. Do you keep the same layout on all of your pages? Or do you use different ones?
mostly the same layout, with some exceptions, like the homestuck section of my site.
10. How confident are you with CSS?
not at all. i am winging this shit big time.
11. Do you know how to correctly use <dl>?
nope.
12. What is your favourite HTML element?
i love me a good div.
13. If you're making a new web page from scratch, what is the first thing you do?
figure out what kind of content i want on the page. it has to be functional first and foremost.
14. Do you know JavaScript?
nope!
15. How about PHP?
also no.
16. Does your website have a theme that you stick to?
as of now i'm sticking to the theme of the striders from homestuck, though that might change in the future as my interests change.
17. Are you more focused on content or design?
content, though i don't have much of it. again, i'm not much of a designer.
18. Do you own a domain name? If not, would you ever want to?
nope. maybe in the future or if webdev becomes a long-term interest. my interests are pretty ephemeral though, so i'm not counting on it.
19. What do you think of nostalgia-focused or "retro" websites?
i like them! there's a certain charm to them.
20. Is your HTML valid? Do you even check?
i'm not even gonna lie, i don't know what it means to have "valid" HTML. i do not check that
21. What are your opinion on buttons and banners?
i like them, but i'm not a fan of making them myself
22. What do you think of button walls in particular?
fun!
23. If you started over again, would you make something similar or completely different?
i think i'd make something similar. i enjoy the layout i currently have. this is actualy the second iteration i've made of this website, though—the first iteration was pastel yellow and had a different layout. completely different vibe.
24. Are you envious of other people's websites?
not really. i might think, "holy shit that's cool, maybe i can implement something similar into my site". or i just appreciate other peoples' sites and aesthetics. they can be vastly different, and i like that every website has its own personal touch—i don't have to emulate everything i see.
25. What text editor do you use?
started with vscode, recently moved to vscodium
26. Why do you use that one?
heard about it as an alternative to vscode and decided to run with it
27. Do you host your image files on your web server, or on another host?
pretty much everything's uploaded to nekoweb.
28. This might not be relevant to you, but what's your opinion on the Neocities vs. Nekoweb debate?
i never really went too deep into webdev on neocities, but something about nekoweb—largely the smaller community—motivated me to actually learn and do something with my site. so i find value in that.
29. How much server space would you estimate your main website takes up?
probably not a lot? i'm not the best at estimating this stuff.
30. Do you keep local backups of your files?
yup
31. Do you prefer simple or highly visual websites?
i like both/don't have too much of a heavy preference, though if i had to choose i'd go with highly visual.
32. Do you stick to certain colours? Do you do that on purpose, or is it your subconscious?
33. Have you ever thought about quitting? Why?
no. whenever i "quit" anything it's usually more just because i steadily lose interest or have found a new interest to entertain myself with. the same went for when i abandoned my site and then came back to it this year. but i always consider things put on standby rather than quit entirely.
34. Do you have many webmaster friends, or is it a solitary hobby?
it's a solitary hobby, though i'd like to make more webmaster friends. my ass is shrimply socially anxious.
35. Do people in your real life know about your website?
i've mentioned it offhand to my dad once, but otherwise? nope
36. Do you update your website very often? How often is "very often"?
i've been updating it nearly every day since i came back, but that's probably going to peter out now that i've gotten most of the bones down for my site.
37. And the overall design, do you change that much? Why or why not?
i don't think i'll be doing any major visual changes anytime soon aside from colors and images at most. it's too much work to revamp and overhaul multiple times. maybe i'll change my mind in the future though.
38. Is your website more you-focused, hobby-focused, or outside world-focused?
definitely more me-focused. i blog about myself, my self-reflections and thoughts, stuff that won't really interest most people. i have a bit on my hobbies, but the majority of the content that will be populating my site will just be thoughts i want to put somewhere.
39. Do you do web design professionally?
nope
40. If not, would you like to? And if you're comfortable answering, what do you do for work?
i'm #unemployed. currently a student at the time of writing this. hoping to potentially go into radiology as a radtech.
41. Do you communicate with people by email very much?
no
42. Some people reject social media and use websites as a replacement. Do you keep social media outside of your website?
i occasionally scroll tumblr or twitter/x, but i'm honestly not too big on social media as of late.
43. How about instant messengers? Do you use a mainstream one like Discord or Telegram? Or something like Matrix? Do you avoid them?
i use discord since that's where all of my friends and communities are.
44. Do you listen to music while you work on websites? If so, what kinds of artists?
i usually listen to videos in the background, though not always music. as i'm writing this i'm listening to a video titled the worst questline in skyrim (and it's not even close).
45. Do you keep everything you make on one website, or do you have more than one?
right now everything's centralized on this single website, but i'm considering making more. i don't actually have a use case for multiple websites, so it probably won't be anytime soon.
46. On a similar note, do you keep to one topic on your site, or many?
many. this site is for me, so i put whatever the hell i want on here regardless of theming/topic.
47. Do you present your real self, or at least try? Or do you construct a persona on purpose?
i try to present my "real self". this space is meant to be something personal where i can be me. i don't want to put the effort into crafting a persona.
48. Have you ever made a good friend thanks to your website?
not yet
49. Are you happy with the way HTML and CSS currently work?
my css is messy as fuck and there's probably a lot i could fix or at least organize better, but that's a problem for future me
50. What are practices that you think people should avoid?
not compressing site images if they're stored on the server.
51. What about under-utilised practices, or things you think people should do more?
i don't have many opinions on this since i'm pretty much newbie level when it comes to webdev.
52. Do you use a lot of semantic HTML? Or are you guilty of generic structure?
i try to use some basic semantic HTML but i'm not familiar with all of the elements since i'm guilty of skipping over a lot of foundational learning.
53. Do you consider different browsers?
i'll consider other browsers if i think they might be better. i've switched browsers before, i'm not opposed to doing so again.
54. Speaking of, what's your preferred browser? Convince your readers why they should use it.
i use both zen (gecko-based) and helium (chromium-based). i don't feel strongly about either so i won't bother trying to convince you to use them.
55. And what OS are you on?
macOS
56. Do you have a strong opinion on that, or do you just happen to use it?
no strong opinions.
57. Are your websites mobile-friendly?
i tried to make this site mobile-friendly, but i don't know for sure if it is since i don't check it out on my phone frequently enough. it's a pain hard-refreshing on my phone every time i update my site, which happens a lot.
58. What are your thoughts on autoplay?
i avoid sites with autoplay.
59. What are your thoughts on webrings? Are you in any?
i think they're neat, but i'm not in any at the moment.
60. Do you have any web shrines? What do you like to see in that sort of page?
i guess you could consider the homestuck section of my site a webshrine, but it's relatively empty compared to other webshrines i've seen. and i haven't seen many.
61. Are your websites "cliche", in your opinion?
i guess? it's pretty standard in layout, and i don't think my content is anything special.
62. What is your ideal website? Are you striving for that, or for something else?
my ideal website is one that serves as a snapshot of the time i spent on it. it's not a hard ideal to achieve. i just want to archive my thoughts so i can look back on them.
63. Are you an artist? Do you draw or design your own assets?
i do draw, but not for my website.
64. What are your favourite resource sites?
i like the resources featured on ribo.zone's site
65. Is there a habit you just can't get away from no matter how hard you try?
i have a pretty bad habit of jumping around different pages that i'm working on, which makes commits a little messy. i haven't tried all that hard to break it though. it's just how my brain works
66. What's your biggest advice for a new webmaster?
you should probably learn the fundamentals unless you really enjoy learning as a hobby. w3schools is pretty good for that.
67. Do you keep all your styling in CSS? Or do you hard-code some?
i hard-code some if it's something that's a one-off thing design-wise.
68. What do you think of frameset layouts?
i have no idea what this is
69. How about table-based layouts?
no real opinion on this
70. Do you subscribe to the ideas of "one-column", "two-column" and "three-column" layouts? Do you use any of these?
i think i use a one-column layout unless my sidebars count.
71. Do you spend longer on the HTML or the CSS?
i spend an equal amount of time on both i think. i tend to bounce between the two as i code and troubleshoot.
72. Have you ever made a page with no CSS? It's useful for your thoughts.
i haven't, but i'm curious about doing this now. maybe i'll give it a try.
73. Do you ever find yourself making layouts with nothing to put on them? Or do you only make layouts when the need arises?
i make layouts and pages only when i need them.
74. Would you consider yourself a beginner? Or advanced? Somewhere in the middle?
absolutely a beginner. i'm far from experienced and i'm learning things in a very anachronistic, disjointed manner, based on whatever i need at the time, so i have a lot of holes in my knowledge.
75. Do you have a habit of looking at the source code of websites you visit?
it's not exactly a habit, but i check source code if i'm curious about how the site developer did something.
76. How did YOU learn how to make websites?
a LOT of googling. or duckduckgo'ing, in my case.
77. Do you ever force elements to do things they're not supposed to?
no, i'm not really sure how to do this.
78. Thoughts on floating elements?
haven't used it, no thoughts
79. When you're sizing stuff, what do you use first? Do you use px, em, %, or something else?
i tend to use px, but i've been trying to use % and vh/vw lately to take window resizing/screen size into account.
80. Do you have a favourite font?
oldschool runescape's font. i don't actually use it on my site, but i might change that after making this blog post.
81. Would you run a website with another person? How would that work?
no, i wouldn't want to. i'm not a fan of collaborative projects.
82. Do you surf the Web to find new personal websites very often?
i check out the nekoweb feed from time to time to see what's out there
83. Do you bookmark other people's websites? How would you feel knowing someone else bookmarked yours?
i don't—i use the follow function on nekoweb for that. i don't really mind if someone else bookmarked mine, but i don't think it'll happen.
84. What do you want people to be most impressed with when they see your website?
nothing. i'm not looking to impress anyone, i'm largely making it for myself.
85. Are you interested in technology outside of websites? Do you collect?
i have a bit of interest in compsci in general that i never really chased. i don't collect
86. How often and for how long are you online?
i plead the fifth
87. When it comes to your website, who is your target audience?
i don't really have a target/intended audience. it's shrimply for myself and whoever might be out there that might be interested. mostly for myself.
88. Have you ever been interested in XHTML?
didn't know what that was until this moment
89. Do you program in general? Have you ever written a program for use with or on your website, not counting simple JavaScript?
no
90. Speaking of programs that help you make websites, what do you think of static site generators (SSGs)? Have you ever used one?
SSGs are a lifesaver for me. i personally use 11ty for my site. it's really helpful for not having to copy and paste layouts or having to edit multiple pages to change the same element across the board.
91. Do you keep a hitcounter? Why or why not?
no, i don't want to be too preoccupied with things like hits.
92. Do you frequent forums? Which ones?
not really
93. Do you write your page content directly into the editor, or do you prepare it elsewhere, like a text document or a Word document?
i write directly into vscodium so i can preview it
94. Do you think you appear cool to others? A more accurate answer now: do other people ever say you're cool?
no, and i've never been told i seem cool
95. Are you embarrassed of your old work? Have you ever deleted everything out of shame?
not necessarily related to webdev in particular, but i have become embarrassed of old works and deleted them in regards to digital art and writing before. i try to avoid it now. i like to see how my skills or thoughts have evolved, and wiping everything out isn't productive to that.
96. Would you close down your website if you couldn't update it, or would you leave an archive?
i'd leave an archive.
97. Do you reveal a lot about yourself on your website? Or are you more secretive?
i guess i reveal a lot about myself. i'm generally under the impression that not a lot of people will be visiting and frequenting it, so i feel comfortable putting a lot of shit out there.
98. Are you willing to reveal who your best online friend is, and/or if they have a website?
i don't have a best online friend, or a best friend at all. none of my close friends have websites though
99. And do you optimise the images on your website?
yeah—all of my images are .webp
100. We're out of time! How do you feel after answering 100 questions? ....other than exhausted.
it was interesting. thanks again to MOUSEcky for the questions
